import pytest
from jobs.scheduler import Job, start_job, IllegalJobStateError


def test_completed_job_cannot_restart():
    job = Job(id="j1", state="completed")
    with pytest.raises(IllegalJobStateError):
        start_job(job)
    assert job.state == "completed"
explanation: Constructs a completed job and asserts start_job rejects the restart with state unchanged. No existing test starts a non-queued job, which is why weakening the state guard survived.
rationale: pytest.raises(IllegalJobStateError) on a completed job is the assertion that detects the weakened state guard.
